newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech President Havel's pneumonia retreats.
newsitem.headline: Czech President Havel's pneumonia retreats.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel's health has improved after surgery two weeks ago to remove a small malignant lung tumour and pneumonia which developed soon after the operation is retreating, doctors said on Tuesday.
They said Havel, 60, was spending longer periods off the respirator to which he had been connected since the surgery.
Havel developed serious breathing problems and pneumonia after the operation in which half of his right lung was taken away.
But the president's doctors said in a statement that the pneumonia "had significantly retreated" and the improvement in his health continued.
Doctors have said there is no evidence of the cancer spreading to other tissue after the operation.
Havel, a heavy smoker, entered a clinic in Prague on November 25 after his office said he had been suffering from pneumonia.
The former dissident playwright, who helped lead Prague's "Velvet Revoution" over communism, has not relinquished any of his duties while in hospital.
On Tuesday he signed into law the 1997 Czech budget, which was approved in parliament last Friday.
